newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese carmakers seen scaling back production.
newsitem.headline: Japanese carmakers seen scaling back production.

text.p: Hit by sluggish car sales at home, Honda Motor Co. Ltd said Friday it would scale back its domestic output for July, and analysts said other Japanese automakers would eventually follow suit and revise down their output plans later in the business year.
Japan's top five carmakers, except for Mazda Motor Corp., suffered a drop in domestic car sales in May even while production grew, helped by higher exports.
Domestic car sales have been affected by an April rise in the national sales tax to 5 percent from 3 percent, which has forced consumers to tighten their purse strings.

"All Japanese carmakers are likely to revise down their domestic car output plans, because the combined total of their projected output is too large," said Seiji Sugiura, an industry analyst at Nomura Securities Co. Ltd's research unit.
"They need to cut their output plans by at least 600,000 units," he said.
Japan's 11 vehicle makers planned total production of 11.33 million vehicles in the current 1997/98 business year, against output of 10.60 million units in the previous year.

"They have to lower their output because their production plans are too optimistic. Overall domestic production is likely to fall by 200,000 or 300,000 units this year, or be flat against last year at the best," Kankaku Research senior analyst Nobuaki Yanachi said.

He said carmakers may reduce their output in the second half of 1997/98 after a build-up in inventories. Domestic inventories fell sharply due to higher sales ahead of the April sales tax increase and strong exports.

On Tuesday, Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Yoshifumi Tsuji said that Japan's domestic sales in the June 1 to June 17 period were down 5 percent from the same period a year ago. He said domestic car sales in 1997/98 were likely to be lower than in the previous year.

A Honda spokesman said Friday that the company would scale back production at its two domestic plants in July in line with slowing domestic orders. But Honda stopped short of saying it would revise down its production plan for the business year.
A Toyota spokesman said the company has no plans to revise its domestic output plan, under which it forecast production of 3.55 million vehicles in 1997/98, up 1.4 percent from 3.50 million.
Nissan Motor Co. Ltd, Mitsubishi Motors Corp. and Mazda also said they have no plans to revise their domestic output estimates because of expected good demand for their new models.
